Let $d=\text{Radial}-\text{Belted}$. The paired differences are

$$0.1,-0.2,0.4,0.1,-0.1,0.1,0,0.2,0.5,0.2,0.1,0.3.$$

They have $\bar d\approx0.14167$ and $s_d\approx0.19752$ km/L.

a. Test

$$H_0:\mu_d=0\quad\text{versus}\quad H_a:\mu_d>0.$$

With $df=11$,

$$t=\frac{0.14167}{0.19752/\sqrt{12}}\approx2.4845.$$

The right-tail p-value is approximately $0.0152$. Since $0.0152<0.05$, reject $H_0$. There is sufficient evidence that radial tires produce better mean fuel economy.

b. With $t_{0.975,11}\approx2.201$,

$$\bar d\pm t_{0.975,11}\frac{s_d}{\sqrt{12}}\approx0.14167\pm0.12550.$$

The 95% confidence interval is approximately **$(0.0162,0.2672)$ km/L**.
